I read it twice. The hard list is the one that knew me. Health, money, the body, the debts, the running about, the part of me that is never at home in itself - yes, all of that, and it says so without being asked. It even says it is unusually sure about courage and about brothers and sisters, and I had a brother I never met who died at fifteen, and a sister I did not know I had until I was nearly grown, and a nerve that fails me on a soundstage in front of people who are paid to wait for me. So it is pointed where my life is bruised, and I will give it that.

But the favourable list is a stranger's life. Home, property and your mother reads well. My mother has been in institutions most of my life and I was passed hand to hand through eleven homes and an orphanage, and I have never in my life had a house I felt was mine. Marriage and partnerships reads well. I have been married three times and I am divorced three times, and I do not think anybody who has watched that would call it favourable. And it says I am steady and self-reliant and happier leading than following - self-reliant, all right, because there was nobody else to rely on, but steady is not a word one person who has known me would use, and it says itself that is only a tendency, so I will not argue with a page.

What I notice is that when it praises, it could be praising anyone, and when it wounds, it is specific. Perhaps that is how these things work. I have been read by people before - palms, cards, a woman in a room off Sunset - and they all told me I would be adored, and they were right, and it did not help. What I would want a page like this to tell me is not which parts of my life read well. It is how to be one person instead of two, and I do not think the stars have that written down anywhere.
